description:
The companies a portfolio owns through its funds, added up across funds: the largest
        names with their share of the whole portfolio, names reached through more than
        one fund, and sectors. Use it for 'what do I really own?'; for the full
        measurement use measure_portfolio, for one fund alone asset_info. Give
        holdings as money amounts to get each company in money; base sets that
        currency (default USD). Figures are minimums: they count only the companies
        the measurement can name, and the answer says how much of the money that is.

base.description: Currency every figure is expressed in (USD, EUR, GBP, CAD…). Default USD.
base.title: Base

holdings.description: What is held: {ticker: weight or amount}. Weights need not sum to one; amounts in the base currency are also accepted (then the crises are shown in money). 1 to 100 holdings. Tickers as the exchange lists them (VOO, VWCE.DE, XAW.TO; 'CASH.USD' for cash).
holdings.title: Holdings

name: look_through

outputSchema.description: What the portfolio owns through its funds.

_fence.description: What these figures are and are not: descriptive, no forecast, no advice. Repeat its sense when presenting the result.

covered_fraction.description: Share of the money whose underlying holdings are visible, 0 to 1.

data.description: Where the prices came from and what was missing or repaired.

as_of.description: Last date of price history used.

missing.description: Tickers with no usable history (left out).

standins.description: Holdings measured through a stand-in with longer history: ticker, proxy, index, from, until, evidence.

duplicated_exposure.description: Share held more than once through different funds.

exposures.description: [company, share of the whole portfolio] pairs, largest first.

opaque.description: Holdings with no breakdown to look through.

refused.description: Funds whose breakdown the data vendor refused.

top_symbol_weight.description: Its share of the whole portfolio.

title: What the funds hold underneath
